title: A/P Summary and Detail count a vendor credit dated on the as-of date in Current
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin user (the "Admin" role).
  • Have a new vendor (created for this test), vendor A, with only these open documents on today's date: a bill A of $500.00, 20 days past due, and an unused vendor credit A of $120.00 dated today.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 px wide.
  • Open A/P Summary (Reports, then "A/P Aging Summary" under ACCOUNTS PAYABLE in the left menu).
  • Leave the report with only vendor A ticked in the Vendor filter.
custom_steps:
1. Read vendor A's row and the Totals row.
  2. Open A/P Detail from the Reports menu.
  3. In the Vendor filter, tick vendor A.
  4. Click the chevron button in the table's top-left header cell (Expand all).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Current $-120.00 and 1-30 Days $500.00; 31-60 Days, 61-90 Days and 91 And Over are blank.
  • Total $380.00 (500.00 − 120.00).
  • The Totals row reads the same: Current $-120.00, 1-30 Days $500.00, Total $380.00.

Step 2:

  • A/P Detail opens on today's date.

Step 3:

  • Vendor A is ticked.

Step 4:

  • "Current" holds vendor credit A with an Open Balance of $-120.00 and Past Due 0.
  • "1-30 days past due" holds bill A with an Open Balance of $500.00.
  • The Totals row's Open Balance reads $380.00: bucket by bucket the same as A/P Summary's Totals.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 11 (5 Nov 2026, Chris Ward), read 10 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11535 (Story 5, Filters: customer or vendor, past due and location)

  • S1-R5a: “A document is Current when its due date is on or after the as-of date. Its Past Due, where the report shows one, is the number of days from the due date to the as-of date: negative while the document is not yet due (a bill due 9 days after the as-of date reads -9, as today) and 0 on its due date. A credit memo, deposit or vendor credit counts its own date as its due date, so one dated exactly on the as-of date is in Current with Past Due 0, not in "1-30 days past due". This is how QuickBooks ages them (SV-11441).”
  • S5-R18a: “For the same as-of date, customer or vendor and Location, with Past due on Any, A/R Summary's Totals equal A/R Detail's Open Balance Totals bucket by bucket, and A/P Summary's equal A/P Detail's. The Detail reports' Amount column holds original amounts and is not compared. With a Past due filter they can differ: a Summary keeps the whole row of a customer or vendor that qualifies (Current and credits included), while a Detail report lists only the invoices or bills that qualify, plus every credit.”
  • S5-R18: “The Totals row always adds up exactly the rows the filters leave (customer or vendor, Past due, Location), on screen on every page, in the PDF and in the CSV. On A/R Collection and A/P Unpaid Invoices this fixes today's Totals row, which ignores the customer or vendor filter.”

Not yet checked against a build: the QA build v26.45.2-6a8b89c exists since 10 Nov 2026 and this case has not been run on it yet.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), version of 5 Nov 2026 (1793886208-34e0), read 10 Nov 2026: page 1 "Opening order and header sorting" (board Main.dc.html); page 4 "Location filter and Location column" (board Location.dc.html); page 7 "Filters and call list" (board Filters.dc.html). The design draws no picture of this behaviour (all 7 boards and 45 figures checked); the case follows the PRD.
